html:
Russian novelist, born in 1828 into a noble family on the estate of Yasnaya Polyana, south of Moscow. He wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina, often ranked among the greatest novels.

He served as an officer in the Crimean War. War and Peace (1869) follows several families through Napoleon's invasion of Russia in 1812. Anna Karenina (1878) tells of a married woman's love affair and its cost, set beside a landowner's search for meaning.

Around 1880 he went through a spiritual crisis. He turned to his own reading of the Gospels: love, simple living and refusing violence, even against evil. He rejected the church, the state and private property. The Russian Orthodox Church excommunicated him in 1901.

His book The Kingdom of God Is Within You deeply moved the young Mahatma Gandhi, and the two wrote to each other; Gandhi named a farm in South Africa after him. He died in 1910 at a railway station, having left home at 82. His rival in fame was Dostoevsky.
sum: Russian novelist, born in 1828 into a noble family on the estate of Yasnaya Polyana, south of Moscow. He wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina, often ranked among the greatest novels.
